targets.text: Jira flow closes its loop: the merged flow-store cycle is deployed and proven on prod records, the spec a ticket is deciding on is readable from the ticket itself as a rendered page, the /think leg can be driven from the board, and the bugs that bit the last cycle (deploy.sh un-granting the sweep, the bridge scope-boundary false denial, the dial-in 401 loop) no longer reproduce
Every leg in the announcement is proven from prod records with no session context, and the cycle ends with a /summarize-delivery record before its PR merges — not ten days after

The flow-store build cycle (#203 / PR #208, 11 of 13 plan tasks) is closed properly before new Jira-flow work opens: a /summarize-delivery record is written (today .devague/deliveries/jira-operating-surface-flow-store.json holds only deviation d1 and docs/deliveries has no entry for the cycle), and #192/#193/#194/#197/#198 close only on t13's live prod proof, not on the merge
The delivery summary docs/deliveries/2026-08-19-jira-operating-surface-flow-store.md is on main, and #192 #193 #194 #197 #198 are closed only by #230's prod-record evidence — never on the merge

The r4 deploy unit (migrations 0041→0045, sweep.py + pr_upkeep_jira.py, adoption-aware control plane, one deploy to thor per migrations/README.md) ships to prod before any Jira-flow leg is proven: GET /v1alpha1/version on prod (192.168.1.146:18080) returns revision c041f28, a pre-squash commit reachable only from origin/scrum2/hands-free-pickup, 12+ commits behind main — none of the history-faithful sweep, re-mint, ticket reports, or comment consumer is running

After the deploy, prod's GET /v1alpha1/version names a revision that contains c0f6c4a, migrations 0041(cutover)–0045 are applied, and the prod registry lists pr-upkeep-sweep-cycle v2 (two-pair bootstrap) and jira-comment-consumer — read back from prod, not from the deploy log

#191 is fixed as part of this cycle: deploy/prod/deploy.sh lines 88-97 rewrite ~/.culture-nodes/runner.env from a fixed block that never writes NODES_API_URL, and line 116-118 defaults PR_UPKEEP_REPOSITORIES to a jira-less document whenever the operator's shell does not re-supply it — the sweep-cycle workflow (examples/pr-upkeep/sweep-cycle.workflow.yaml:99-104) names both as environment_refs, so every deploy either fail-closes the sweep or amputates its Jira source silently; the fix re-grants both (or refuses to deploy without them) and is what makes the r4 deploy safe

Two consecutive deploy.sh runs against a host whose runner.env already carries NODES_API_URL and a jira-bearing PR_UPKEEP_REPOSITORIES leave both intact (or the deploy refuses loudly before touching the file), and a named test drives the env-writing section against a fake host to prove it

The /think leg runs Jira-driven (#199, plan task t10): examples/spec-chain/workflow.yaml (22 nodes, compiles, unpublished, unwired) is published and reachable from a ticket fact, frame decisions land as marked questions on the ticket, and the human's reply transacts exactly the stated decision — confirmations stay user-only

On prod records: a spec-chain run whose trigger_event_id is a ticket-derived fact; a frame decision posted as a marked question, answered on the board, transacts exactly the stated devague move and nothing else; the run mutates .devague/ only through the declared owe-developer custody

#207 is fixed: the claude bridge's workflow-scope boundary measures the committed diff against the branch base, not the whole workspace delta, so a step-0 base move no longer produces a false policy_denied (run 01M0DYPYFTWRWF3AXH24PD9FXF) — every developer dispatch in this cycle that syncs its checkout otherwise needs the operator to pre-sync the worktree by hand (hand-turn 5 on #203)

Named tests pin both sides: a session whose step-0 base move drags .github changes ends completed, and a session that itself edits .github/ still ends policy_denied; one live developer dispatch with a base move completes without operator pre-sync

#205 is fixed: the culture-nodes-claude-developer bridge on spark stops its once-per-second 401 dial-in reconnect loop (backoff plus a correct dial-in credential), so dial-in coverage on the developer lane is real rather than silently dead

One hour of the developer bridge's journal after the fix shows dial-in reconnects backing off and no sustained 401 loop, and /v1alpha1/dial-in-presence lists the developer bridge; the fix is one dialin.py propagated byte-identically to all five adapters

#202 needs no new work: pr-upkeep v11 declares ledger.propose [claim] and three v11 runs completed honestly on prod (#203 comment 2026-08-19T23:22Z) — it closes on that evidence, and the same trap is checked across the other published workflows rather than re-fixed

#202 is closed citing the three v11 completed runs on prod (#203 comment 2026-08-19T23:22Z) and a one-line audit that every published workflow's actor nodes declare a ledger.propose block — no code change

Session economics hold (#48, CLAUDE.md split-plan lane): build packages route to codex/developer actors through /nodes-operator assign, the operator's Claude window is reserved for merge gates, deploy, and the t13 proof, and every hand-turn gets an issue comment

The split plan declares model-session counts per wave before any dispatch, every build package is dispatched through nodes-operator assign, and every operator hand-turn is a comment on #230 or the issue it touches

The operator working from the Jira board (files, answers, decides, and reads the spec on the ticket with no repo access); the culture-nodes actor fleet on the developer and codex lanes that builds the legs; and the operator lane that ships the r4 deploy and runs the t13 proof
Each audience can run its leg alone: the operator from the board with no repo access, the fleet from dispatched briefs, the operator lane from deploy.sh plus prod reads

Today prod runs c041f28 (pre-#208): the history-faithful sweep, bounded re-mint, ticket reports and comment consumer exist only on main; the spec a ticket decides on lives only in the checkout (SCRUM-3 comments 10111/10113 summarized 13 claims in prose); the /think leg is the operator session polling the board; every deploy silently un-grants the sweep's NODES_API_URL and Jira config (#191); developer dispatches that sync their base get a false policy_denied (#207) and the developer bridge loops 401 once a second (#205)

Each before-state fact is re-measurable today: prod /v1alpha1/version = c041f28, the prod registry has no jira-comment-consumer, deploy.sh:88-97 has no NODES_API_URL line, #207 and #205 reproduce as their issues describe

A merged-but-undeployed cycle is indistinguishable from a delivered one until someone measures prod — the flow-store cycle went ten days without a delivery record and its five feature issues read as done. Closing the loop on prod, and making the ticket carry the spec, is what lets the board be a peer operating surface instead of a place the operator session polls
The next cycle's delivery summary exists before its PR merges, and the flow-store issues #192–#198 stay open until #230 cites prod records

Prod's /v1alpha1/version names a revision containing c0f6c4a and the prod registry lists pr-upkeep-sweep-cycle v2 and jira-comment-consumer; a real ticket carries one in-place-updated HTML spec page from intake to PR merge; a ticket fact mints the spec chain and a marked question answered on the board transacts exactly that frame move; deploy.sh preserves the sweep's grants; #207 and #205 no longer reproduce; #192 #193 #194 #197 #198 are closed on prod evidence via #230
Every item in the after-state maps to a numbered success signal in c18 that a reader can re-measure from prod without this session

Measured from prod records with no session context: (1) GET /v1alpha1/version revision contains c0f6c4a; (2) a two-comment reply on a real ticket emits two facts in order; (3) the ticket shows one spec page whose content changed across at least two lane milestones without a second attachment appearing; (4) a spec-chain run id whose trigger_event_id is a ticket fact; (5) two consecutive deploy.sh runs leave NODES_API_URL and the jira half of PR_UPKEEP_REPOSITORIES intact in runner.env; (6) a developer dispatch with a base move ends completed; (7) one hour of developer-bridge journal with no 401 loop

Every one of the seven signals is recorded in the cycle's delivery summary with the prod read (URL or command plus output) that measured it; a signal that cannot be measured is recorded as unverified, never asserted

The ticket page (#200, redefined): the web UI gains a /tickets/<ticket-id> route rendering the ticket's whole conversation from control-plane state — spec claims with confirmation state, questions/decisions, start/finish reports, run status, and the reply thread — with a link back to the Jira ticket; the page's URL is posted on the ticket at intake through the jira bridge and replaced in place, never duplicated; a reply submitted on the page is posted as a Jira comment via the bridge under the system's account and appended as a human engine fact, and the page freezes with a pointer to the merged PR; the render is deterministic from state, no LLM in the path

On a real ticket: the ticket carries one link to /tickets/<id> posted at intake; the page opened with no repo access shows every claim with its state and the reply thread; one reply typed on the page appears as a Jira comment on the ticket AND as an engine fact that resumes a waiting flow, measured from prod records; the same state renders byte-identically twice; the UI's PRD §8.8 accessibility rules (keyboard order, icon+word status, reduced motion) hold on the new route

The r4 deploy unit is TWO deploys, not one: deploy.sh thor (migrate → nodes-cutover → stack) then deploy.sh orin, with orin's worker stopped before thor's migrate/cutover window and restarted after, and revision parity verified (prod GET /v1alpha1/version vs each worker image's REVISION) before the sweep schedule resumes — deploy.sh:703 stops thor's services only and no api↔worker revision check exists (migrations_test.go:24-27 records the one-host premise as false)

Prod records after r4 show thor's api and both workers at one revision containing c0f6c4a, and no 'Jira history cutover is pending' delivery errors (internal/store/postgres/signal.go:705) in the deploy window

Rollback for r4 is restore-from-dump, not schema rollback (no down migrations; docs/adr/0002 N-1 promise does not cover a 12-commit jump): deploy.sh takes a fresh pg dump immediately before migrate and the summary names it, so a bad 0041→0045 apply is recoverable per deploy/prod/RESTORE.md
~/.culture-nodes/backups/ on thor holds a dump timestamped after the sweep stop and before migrate, and the restore procedure was rehearsed once against it (dry run) before the real deploy

The re-mint scheduler's producer actor id engine_remint_scheduler (internal/engine/remint.go:21-28, RemintProducerActorID unwired in cmd/nodes/worker.go) is registered in prod's actors table before r4, or every due re-mint fails its ledger append (actors(id) FK) on the first technical failure after deploy
GET /v1alpha1/actors on prod lists engine_remint_scheduler before the first post-deploy sweep, and the first re-mint's derived record appends without an FK error

A page reply enters the engine through a NEW server-side endpoint (POST /v1alpha1/tickets/{id}/replies) guarded the way human-task decisions are (NODES_HUMAN_DECISION_TOKEN_SECRET, browser token in sessionStorage per web/src/api/decision-token.ts) with a required replier field like decider_actor_id: the endpoint appends the fact in-process with origin.kind human and the replier named, then mirrors it to Jira via the bridge's post_comment as 'via <replier>' — the browser never holds NODES_EVENT_TOKEN_SECRET (namespace-wide emit standing, signalevents.go:226-252)

One reply typed on the page yields exactly one engine fact (origin.kind human, replier set) and one Jira comment; the sweep's next pass emits nothing for that comment (self-echo by account id, pr_upkeep_jira.py:100-113); a GET /v1alpha1/events stream shows no second fact

The mirrored Jira comment is display-only: the sweep swallows it by design (account-id self-echo is authoritative, hardened after incident s14) and the self-echo contract is NOT carved out for page replies; a human who types directly in Jira still reaches the engine via the sweep, and both paths produce the same fact name and payload shape so consumers never fork on origin
A named test asserts the page-reply fact and the sweep-emitted comment fact validate against one schema, and jira_comment_is_self_echo is unchanged

The SPA never carries a namespace-wide secret (NODES_EVENT_TOKEN_SECRET, actor tokens, the jira bridge bearer); the only browser-held standing stays the typed, sessionStorage-only decision token; the ticket page is not offered beyond the LAN until an auth story exists (park v4)
grep of web/src for every *_SECRET / bearer name returns only the decision-token path

The ticket page has a server-side source: GET /v1alpha1/tickets/{id} composes runs by subject (a new subject filter on listRuns — runs.subject exists per migration 0038 but is not a query filter), their ledger and human tasks, ticket-report outbox rows, page replies, AND a frame snapshot — no .devague/ state is in the control plane today (internal/devague only parses delivery fixtures; MapFrameClaims has zero callers), so the /think leg publishes its frame (claims with state, questions, decisions) into the control plane after each move as a new versioned record keyed by ticket id
GET /v1alpha1/tickets/SCRUM-N on prod returns the frame snapshot whose claim states match devague show --json in the lane worktree at the same move, plus the runs whose subject is SCRUM-N

(8) On prod records: a reply submitted through /tickets/<ticket-id> with the decision token appears as one Jira comment on the ticket authored by the system account 'via <replier>', one engine fact with origin.kind human and the replier named, and a previously waiting run whose resume cites that fact's id — and the next sweep pass emits no fact for the mirrored comment
Signal 8 is recorded in the cycle's delivery summary with the ticket key, the comment id, the fact id, and the resumed run id read from prod — or marked unverified

(9) Across at least two lane milestones on a real ticket, exactly one comment carrying the page-link marker exists on the ticket (edited or re-posted in place), its URL path contains the ticket id, and the page it points at links back to the ticket — counted from the ticket's comment list, not from attachments
Signal 9 is recorded with the ticket's comment list at two milestones (ids and marker), showing one link comment — or marked unverified

tasks.summary: Reply endpoint: POST /v1alpha1/tickets/{id}/replies (guarded by a replier-BOUND bearer derived from NODES_HUMAN_DECISION_TOKEN_SECRET — the token names the replier and the server verifies the binding, so the required replier field is checked against the token rather than trusted; required client-generated reply_id) appends a signal event in-process with origin.kind human and the AUTHENTICATED replier named, and enqueues a display-only mirror comment 'via <replier>' through the jira bridge outbox — the fact and its mirror row are written in ONE store transaction and the request is idempotent on reply_id; the page-reply fact and the sweep's comment fact validate against one schema
acceptance_criteria: PG-backed test with a DECOY run: two runs parked on the same until.signal name, one whose subject is the fixture ticket and one whose subject is a different ticket; one POST yields exactly one signal_events row (origin.kind human, replier in payload, and the ticket id + originating_question_id in the same payload fields the sweep's comment fact carries) and one outbox row. A signal park matches (namespace, event_name) only, with no subject or payload filter (internal/store/postgres/signal.go selectLockedSubscriptionsSQL; examples/jira-question-round-trip/question_correlation.py states this contract), so BOTH subscriptions fire: the test asserts the ticket's run resumes and its resume cites the fact id, AND that the decoy run's consumer gets answer_for(payload, its_question_id) == None and re-parks without acting — the cross-ticket wake is observed and neutralised, not assumed away
A schema test validates a fixture page-reply fact and a fixture sweep comment fact against the same JSON Schema
jira_comment_is_self_echo in examples/pr-upkeep/pr_upkeep_jira.py is unchanged (test pins its bytes)

Atomic dual write: the fact and its mirror row are written by ONE store method (e.g. Store.DeliverPageReply) that calls the private tx-aware seam deliverSignalEventTx (internal/store/postgres/signal.go; FireSchedule is the precedent, t33 criterion 2) and inserts the mirror row inside the SAME transaction — the handler never calls the public DeliverSignalEvent (which begins and commits its own transaction) and then inserts the mirror as a second statement. Failure-injection PG test: with the mirror insert made to fail (a fixture that violates the mirror table's constraint), the POST returns 5xx and afterwards there are ZERO signal_events rows and ZERO mirror rows for that reply — never a fact without a mirror

Idempotent retry: the request carries a required client-generated reply_id (400 without it); the store delivers with SourceKey 'page-reply:{ticket id}:{reply_id}' and Watermark {"reply_id": ...} — a shape jiraHistoryIssueSourceKey does not recognise, so the pre-cutover suppression is not tripped — and the mirror row is UNIQUE on the fact id it mirrors (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). Retry test: the same POST twice yields exactly one signal_events row and one mirror row, both responses cite the same fact id and the second carries duplicate: true. The mirror cannot reuse jira_ticket_report_outbox unchanged (migrations/0043: run_id and trigger_event_id NOT NULL, phase CHECKed to start|finish, UNIQUE (run_id, phase)); expand it or add a sibling table — the invariant is the unique key on the fact id, not the table

Identity binding: the route does NOT reuse requireDecisionAuth as-is — the deployment-wide decision secret authorizes an operation but names no principal (internal/api/humantasks.go; decider_actor_id is passed through unverified the same way, which web/src/api/decision-token.ts documents as the phase-1 posture). The reply route requires a replier-bound bearer of the form '<replier>.<hex HMAC-SHA256(NODES_HUMAN_DECISION_TOKEN_SECRET, "page-reply:" + replier)>', verified by a new requireReplierAuth that recomputes the MAC for the presented replier and compares SHA-256 digests in constant time (the requireDecisionAuth pattern); the recorded replier is the token's replier, and the body's required replier must equal it (403 on mismatch). Minting is operator-side from the secret — a Go helper in internal/api that the tests call, and a documented openssl one-liner that produces the same bytes — so a person holds only their own bound token and can derive nobody else's; the browser never holds the secret. Negative tests, each asserting ZERO signal_events rows and ZERO mirror rows afterwards: a token bound to 'alice' with body replier 'bob' → 403; the plain deployment-wide decision secret as bearer → 401; no bearer → 401. Positive test: alice's token with replier alice → the fact's payload names alice and the outbox row's comment reads 'via alice'. api/openapi/openapi.yaml documents the bound-token scheme on this route as distinct from the decision bearer

tasks.summary: Link at intake and freeze: jira-intake's intake node posts ONE page-link comment and keeps it single across milestones through a NEW narrow bridge verb upsert_comment (adapters/jira: mapping/client know only post_comment today — no lookup, edit, or comment id; verbs are dispatched by isinstance in server.py, transition_issue is the precedent for a second verb): input is exactly {verb, issue, comment, link_key}; the bridge GETs the issue's comments, finds the one authored by its own account carrying the marker [culture-nodes:jira-actor link=<link_key>], PUTs /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment/{id} if found and POSTs otherwise, and returns {issue, comment_id, action: created|updated} — the comment id is recovered from Jira by marker lookup on every run, never persisted in the control plane, so a re-run needs no state to stay single; examples/jira-intake's post-comment node switches to upsert_comment with link_key = the ticket id; the sweep emits pr.merged for closed PRs with merged_at (watermarked) and links the PR to its ticket by branch name or body carrying the ticket id; a pr.merged fact freezes the ticket's page (frozen flag + merged PR pointer on the projection)
acceptance_criteria: Sweep test: a merged PR yields exactly one pr.merged fact across two passes (watermark), with issue_key parsed from the branch or body; an open PR yields none
